algorithms.name: parse a CSS <color> value
algorithms.html: To parse a CSS <color> value, given a string input, and an optional context element element:

steps.html: Parse input as a <color>. If the result is failure, return failure; otherwise, let color be the result.

Let used color be the result of resolving color to a used color. If the value of other properties on the element a <color> is on is required to do the resolution (such as resolving a currentcolor or system color), use element if it was passed, or the initial values of the properties if not.
Return used color.

algorithms.html: Conversion to the polar form is trivial:

steps.html: C = sqrt(a^2 + b^2)
if (C > epsilon) H = atan2(b, a) else H is missing
L is the same

algorithms.html: Conversion to the rectangular form is trivial:

steps.html: If H is missing, H = 0
ignored: a = C cos(H) b = C sin(H)

steps.html: L is the same

algorithms.html:
For all predefined RGB color spaces,
	conversion to Lab requires several steps,
	although in practice all but the first step are linear calculations and can be combined.

steps.html: Convert from gamma-encoded RGB to linear-light RGB (undo gamma encoding)
Convert from linear RGB to CIE XYZ

If needed, convert from a D65 whitepoint (used by sRGB, display-p3, a98-rgb and rec2020) to the D50 whitepoint used in Lab, with the linear Bradford transform. prophoto-rgb already has a D50 whitepoint.
Convert D50-adapted XYZ to Lab

algorithms.html: Conversion to Oklab is similar, but the chromatic adaptation step is only needed for prophoto-rgb.

steps.html: Convert from gamma-encoded RGB to linear-light RGB (undo gamma encoding)
Convert from linear RGB to CIE XYZ
If needed, convert from a D50 whitepoint (used by prophoto-rgb) to the D65 whitepoint used in Oklab, with the linear Bradford transform.
Convert D65-adapted XYZ to Oklab

algorithms.html: Conversion from Lab to predefined spaces like display-p3 or rec2020 also requires multiple steps, and again in practice all but the last step are linear calculations and can be combined.

steps.html: Convert Lab to (D50-adapted) XYZ
If needed, convert from a D50 whitepoint (used by Lab) to the D65 whitepoint used in sRGB and most other RGB spaces, with the linear Bradford transform. prophoto-rgb' does not require this step.
Convert from (D65-adapted) CIE XYZ to linear RGB
Convert from linear-light RGB to RGB (do gamma encoding)

algorithms.html: Conversion from Oklab is similar, but the chromatic adaptation step is only needed for prophoto-rgb.

steps.html: Convert Oklab to (D65-adapted) XYZ
If needed, convert from a D65 whitepoint (used by Oklab) to the D50 whitepoint used in prophoto-rgb, with the linear Bradford transform.
Convert from (D65-adapted) CIE XYZ to linear RGB
Convert from linear-light RGB to RGB (do gamma encoding)

algorithms.html: Conversion from one predefined RGB color space to another requires multiple steps, one of which is only needed when the whitepoints differ. To convert from src to dest:

steps.html: Convert from gamma-encoded srcRGB to linear-light srcRGB (undo gamma encoding)
Convert from linear srcRGB to CIE XYZ
If src and dest have different whitepoints, convert the XYZ value from srcWhite to destWhite with the linear Bradford transform.
Convert from CIE XYZ to linear destRGB
Convert from linear-light destRGB to destRGB (do gamma encoding)

algorithms.name: prepare a color col1 for conversion
algorithms.html: To <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-export="" id="prepare-a-color-col1-for-conversion" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">prepare a color <var>col1</var> for conversion</dfn>:

steps.html: Change any powerless components in src to missing components
If src is in a cylindrical polar color representation, convert col1 to the corresponding rectangular orthogonal color representation and let this be the new col1.

algorithms.name: convert a color
algorithms.html: To convert a color col1 in a source color space src with white point src-white to a color col2 in destination color space dest with white point dest-white, where src and dest are different:

steps.html: prepare <var>col1</var> for conversion
Replace any missing component with zero.
If src is not a linear-light representation, convert it to linear light (undo gamma-encoding) and let this be the new col1.
Convert col1 to CIE XYZ with a given whitepoint src-white and let this be xyz.
If dest-white is not the same as src-white, chromatically adapt xyz to dest-white using a linear Bradford chromatic adaptation transform, and let this be the new xyz.
If dest is a cylindrical polar color representation, let dest-rect be the corresponding rectangular orthogonal color representation. Otherwise, let dest-rect be dest.
Convert xyz to dest, followed by applying any transfer function (gamma encoding), producing col2.
If dest is a physical output color space, such as a display, then col2 must be css gamut mapped so that it can be displayed.
If dest-rect is not the same as dest, in other words dest is a cylindrical polar color representation, convert from dest-rect to dest, and let this be col2. This may produce missing components.

algorithms.html: Given two <color> values C1 and C2, they are equivalent colors if and only if the following algorithm returns true:

steps.html: For each of C1 and C2, convert any powerless components to missing components.
If C1 and C2 share the same <color-space>:

Compare their components one by one, including the alpha channel. A missing component is only equal to another missing component. Two numeric components are considered equal if they differ by no more than a small implementation-defined ε.

Return true if and only if
					all components compare as equal.
Otherwise, C1 and C2 are in different <color-space>s. If either color has at least one missing component, return false.

Otherwise, neither color has any missing component. Convert both C1 and C2 to oklab, then return true if and only if all components (including alpha) of the converted colors compare as equal, using a standardized Oklab ε of 0.00001.

algorithms.name: to gamut map a color by binary search with local MINDE
algorithms.html:
To <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-export="" id="binary-search-gamut-map-with-local-minde" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">Binary Search Gamut Map with Local MINDE</dfn> a color <var>origin</var>
	in color space <var>origin color space</var>
	to be in gamut of a destination color space <var>destination</var>:

steps.html: if <var>destination</var> has no gamut limits (XYZ-D65, XYZ-D50, Lab, LCH, Oklab, OkLCh) convert <var>origin</var> to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color

let <var>origin_OkLCh</var> be <var>origin</var> converted
		from <var>origin color space</var> to the OkLCh color space

if the Lightness of <var>origin_OkLCh</var> is greater than or equal to 100%,
		convert `oklab(1 0 0 / origin.alpha)` to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color

if the Lightness of <var>origin_OkLCh</var> is less than than or equal to 0%,
		convert `oklab(0 0 0 / origin.alpha)` to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color
if inGamut(<var>origin_OkLCh</var>) is true, convert <var>origin_OkLCh</var> to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color
otherwise, let delta(<var>one</var>, <var>two</var>) be a function which returns the deltaEOK of color <var>one</var> compared to color <var>two</var>
let <var>JND</var> be 0.02
let <var>epsilon</var> be 0.0001
set <var>current</var> to <var>origin_OkLCh</var>
set <var>clipped</var> to clip(<var>current</var>)
set <var>E</var> to delta(<var>clipped</var>, <var>current</var>)
if <var>E</var> < <var>JND</var>
return <var>clipped</var> as the gamut mapped color
set <var>min</var> to zero
set <var>max</var> to the OkLCh chroma of <var>origin_OkLCh</var>
let <var>min_inGamut</var> be a boolean that represents when <var>min</var> is still in gamut, and set it to true
while (<var>max</var> - <var>min</var> is greater than <var>epsilon</var>) repeat the following steps
set <var>chroma</var> to (<var>min</var> + <var>max</var>) /2
set the chroma component of <var>current</var> to <var>chroma</var>
if <var>min_inGamut</var> is true and also if inGamut(<var>current</var>) is true, set <var>min</var> to <var>chroma</var> and continue to repeat these steps
otherwise, carry out these steps:
set <var>clipped</var> to clip(<var>current</var>)
set <var>E</var> to delta(<var>clipped</var>, <var>current</var>)
if <var>E</var> < <var>JND</var>
if (<var>JND</var> - <var>E</var> < <var>epsilon</var>) return <var>clipped</var> as the gamut mapped color
otherwise,
set <var>min_inGamut</var> to false
set <var>min</var> to <var>chroma</var>
otherwise, set <var>max</var> to <var>chroma</var> and continue to repeat these steps
return <var>clipped</var> as the gamut mapped color

algorithms.name: to construct an EdgeSeeker lookup table
algorithms.html:
To <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-export="" id="construct-an-edgeseeker-lookup-table" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">construct an EdgeSeeker lookup table</dfn>
	for an RGB destination color space <var>destination</var>
	with non-imaginary primaries (not, for example, ProPhoto RGB),
	given a number of hue samples per region <var>N</var> (for example, 400):

steps.html: let <var>cusps</var> and <var>curve</var> each be an empty list

for each of the six 60deg hue regions
		(0deg to 60deg, 60deg to 120deg, and so on up to 300deg to 360deg):
let <var>regionCusps</var> and <var>regionCurve</var> each be an empty list

for each of <var>N</var> hues <var>h</var> evenly spaced across that region,
				inclusive of both endpoints, in increasing order:
let r, g and b be the result of converting the HSL triplet (h, 100%, 50%) to RGB using the HSL to RGB conversion

let <var>cusp</var> be the color with coordinates <var>r</var>, <var>g</var>, <var>b</var> in <var>destination</var>,
						converted to the OkLCh color space
append {l: <var>cusp</var>’s Lightness, c: <var>cusp</var>’s Chroma, h: <var>cusp</var>’s Hue} to <var>regionCusps</var>
let r2, g2 and b2 be the result of converting the HSL triplet (h, 100%, 75%) to RGB using the HSL to RGB conversion

let <var>curvePoint</var> be the color with coordinates <var>r2</var>, <var>g2</var>, <var>b2</var> in <var>destination</var>,
						converted to the OkLCh color space

append {l: <var>curvePoint</var>’s Lightness, c: <var>curvePoint</var>’s Chroma, h: <var>curvePoint</var>’s Hue}
						to <var>regionCurve</var>
remove hue folds from regionCusps, and from regionCurve

append every entry of <var>regionCusps</var> except the last to <var>cusps</var>,
				and every entry of <var>regionCurve</var> except the last to <var>curve</var>
sort <var>cusps</var> and <var>curve</var> each by ascending hue
for each of <var>cusps</var> and <var>curve</var>:

let <var>last</var> be its highest-hue entry,
				and let <var>first</var> be its lowest-hue entry with 360deg added to its hue

let <var>end</var> be the entry whose Lightness and Chroma are obtained by
				linearly interpolating, by hue, between <var>last</var> and <var>first</var>
				at hue 360deg

prepend to the list an entry with <var>end</var>’s Lightness and Chroma at hue 0deg,
				and append <var>end</var> at hue 360deg
let <var>LUT</var> be an empty list
for each entry <var>cusp</var> in <var>cusps</var>:

let <var>curvePoint</var> be the entry whose Lightness and Chroma are obtained by
				linearly interpolating, by hue,
				between the two entries in <var>curve</var>
				whose hues most closely bracket <var>cusp</var>’s hue
let curvature be the result of calculating the curvature for cusp and curvePoint
append {l: <var>cusp</var>’s l, c: <var>cusp</var>’s c, h: <var>cusp</var>’s h, curvature: <var>curvature</var>} to <var>LUT</var>
return <var>LUT</var>

algorithms.name: to remove hue folds from a list of EdgeSeeker samples
algorithms.html:
To remove hue folds from a list samples of OkLCh entries in order of increasing sampled HSL hue:

Because the entries are keyed by OkLCh hue, a monotonically increasing sequence of sampled HSL hues does not always produce a monotonically increasing sequence of OkLCh hues: the boundary can fold back on itself. Simply discarding each entry whose hue does not advance keeps the overshoot before the fold and discards the good entries after it, which is worse than doing nothing. Instead, the overshoot is removed, and the boundary resumes at the end of the backward run.

Here the hue step from hue a to hue b is (b − a) modulo 360deg, in the range [0deg, 360deg), and it is forward if it is less than or equal to 180deg.

steps.html: let <var>kept</var> be a list containing the first entry of <var>samples</var>
let <var>i</var> be 1
while <var>i</var> is less than the number of entries in <var>samples</var>:
let <var>j</var> be <var>i</var>
let <var>resume</var> be <var>samples</var>[<var>j</var>]

let <var>first</var> be the index of the first entry of <var>kept</var>
				whose hue step to <var>resume</var>’s hue is not forward,
				that is, the first kept entry past <var>resume</var>’s hue
Assert: there is such an entry, and <var>first</var> is at least 1

let <var>bridge</var> be the entry at hue <var>resume</var>’s hue − 0.0001deg
				whose Lightness and Chroma are obtained by
				linearly interpolating, by hue, between <var>kept</var>[<var>first</var> − 1] and <var>kept</var>[<var>first</var>],
				with the interpolation factor clamped to [0, 1]
remove <var>kept</var>[<var>first</var>] and every entry after it from <var>kept</var>

if the hue step from the hue of the last entry of <var>kept</var> to <var>bridge</var>’s hue
				is forward and not 0deg, append <var>bridge</var> to <var>kept</var>
append <var>resume</var> to <var>kept</var>
set <var>i</var> to <var>j</var> + 1
replace the contents of <var>samples</var> with <var>kept</var>

algorithms.name: to calculate the curvature of a gamut boundary section
algorithms.html:
To calculate the curvature of a gamut boundary section, given a cusp point cusp (the OkLCh Lightness and Chroma of the point of highest chroma for a hue) and a second point curvePoint on the lighter part of the boundary at the same hue:

The boundary section is normalized into a unit square in which (0, 0) is white and (1, 1) is the cusp. The curvature is that of the circle which passes through those two points and through the normalized curvePoint.

steps.html: let <var>x</var> be (100% − <var>curvePoint</var>’s Lightness) / (100% − <var>cusp</var>’s Lightness)
let <var>y</var> be <var>curvePoint</var>’s Chroma / <var>cusp</var>’s Chroma
if <var>x</var> equals <var>y</var>, return 0
let <var>p1</var> be the point (0, 0)
let <var>p2</var> be the point (<var>x</var>, <var>y</var>)
let <var>p3</var> be the point (1, 1)

let <var>m1</var> be
		−1 / ((<var>p2</var>’s y − <var>p1</var>’s y) / (<var>p2</var>’s x − <var>p1</var>’s x)),
		the slope of the perpendicular bisector of the segment from <var>p1</var> to <var>p2</var>

let <var>m2</var> be
		−1 / ((<var>p3</var>’s y − <var>p1</var>’s y) / (<var>p3</var>’s x − <var>p1</var>’s x)),
		the slope of the perpendicular bisector of the segment from <var>p1</var> to <var>p3</var>
let <var>mid1</var> be the midpoint of <var>p1</var> and <var>p2</var>
let <var>mid2</var> be the midpoint of <var>p1</var> and <var>p3</var>

let <var>centerX</var> be
		(<var>m1</var> × <var>mid1</var>’s x − <var>m2</var> × <var>mid2</var>’s x + <var>mid2</var>’s y − <var>mid1</var>’s y) / (<var>m1</var> − <var>m2</var>)
let <var>centerY</var> be <var>m1</var> × (<var>centerX</var> − <var>mid1</var>’s x) + <var>mid1</var>’s y
let <var>radius</var> be sqrt(<var>centerX</var>² + <var>centerY</var>²)
let <var>curvature</var> be 1 / <var>radius</var>
if <var>centerX</var> is less than <var>centerY</var>, return −<var>curvature</var>
return <var>curvature</var>

algorithms.name: to gamut map a color by EdgeSeeker
algorithms.html:
To <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-export="" id="edgeseeker-gamut-map" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">EdgeSeeker Gamut Map</dfn> a color <var>origin</var>
	in color space <var>origin color space</var>
	to be in gamut of an RGB destination color space <var>destination</var>
	with non-imaginary primaries (not, for example, ProPhoto RGB),
	given an EdgeSeeker lookup table <var>LUT</var>
	previously constructed for <var>destination</var>:

steps.html: if <var>destination</var> has no gamut limits (XYZ-D65, XYZ-D50, Lab, LCH, Oklab, OkLCh) convert <var>origin</var> to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color
if <var>destination</var> is HSL or HWB, let <var>LUT</var> be the lookup table constructed for sRGB
if <var>origin</var> is in gamut of <var>destination</var>, return clip(<var>origin</var>)

let <var>origin_OkLCh</var> be <var>origin</var> converted
		from <var>origin color space</var> to the OkLCh color space

if the Lightness of <var>origin_OkLCh</var> is greater than or equal to 100%,
		convert `oklab(1 0 0 / origin.alpha)` to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color

if the Lightness of <var>origin_OkLCh</var> is less than or equal to 0%,
		convert `oklab(0 0 0 / origin.alpha)` to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color
let <var>l</var>, <var>c</var> and <var>h</var> be the Lightness, Chroma and Hue of <var>origin_OkLCh</var>, respectively
if h is missing, set h to 0deg
let maxChroma be the result of finding the maximum chroma for l and h, using LUT
if <var>c</var> is greater than <var>maxChroma</var>, set <var>c</var> to <var>maxChroma</var>

let <var>mapped</var> be the OkLCh color with Lightness <var>l</var>, Chroma <var>c</var>, hue <var>h</var>
		and the same alpha as <var>origin</var>
set <var>clipped</var> to clip(<var>mapped</var>)
return <var>clipped</var> as the gamut mapped color

algorithms.name: to find the maximum in-gamut OkLCh chroma using an EdgeSeeker lookup table
algorithms.html:
To <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-noexport="" id="find-the-maximum-chroma" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">find the maximum chroma</dfn>
	for a given OkLCh Lightness <var>l</var> and hue <var>h</var>,
	using an EdgeSeeker lookup table <var>LUT</var>
	(a list of entries, each with a Lightness, a Chroma, a hue and a curvature,
	sorted by ascending hue and together spanning
	the full hue range from 0deg to 360deg inclusive):

steps.html: if <var>l</var> is less than or equal to 0%, or <var>l</var> is greater than or equal to 100%, return 0

set <var>h</var> to <var>h</var> modulo 360deg,
		adding 360deg to the result if it is negative,
		so that <var>h</var> is in the range [0deg, 360deg)

let <var>lower</var> and <var>upper</var> be the two entries in <var>LUT</var>
		whose hues most closely bracket <var>h</var>,
		such that <var>lower</var>’s hue is less than or equal to <var>h</var>
		and <var>upper</var>’s hue is greater than or equal to <var>h</var>

let <var>t</var> be (<var>h</var> − <var>lower</var>’s hue) / (<var>upper</var>’s hue − <var>lower</var>’s hue),
		or 0 if <var>lower</var> and <var>upper</var> have the same hue

let <var>cuspLightness</var> be
		<var>lower</var>’s Lightness + <var>t</var> × (<var>upper</var>’s Lightness − <var>lower</var>’s Lightness)

let <var>cuspChroma</var> be
		<var>lower</var>’s Chroma + <var>t</var> × (<var>upper</var>’s Chroma − <var>lower</var>’s Chroma)

let <var>curvature</var> be
		<var>lower</var>’s curvature + <var>t</var> × (<var>upper</var>’s curvature − <var>lower</var>’s curvature)

if <var>l</var> is less than or equal to <var>cuspLightness</var>,
		return (<var>l</var> / <var>cuspLightness</var>) × <var>cuspChroma</var>
let <var>x</var> be (100% − <var>l</var>) / (100% − <var>cuspLightness</var>)
return cuspChroma × the result of finding the normalized chroma on the upper gamut boundary arc for x and curvature

algorithms.name: to find the normalized chroma on the upper gamut boundary arc
algorithms.html:
To find the normalized chroma on the upper gamut boundary arc, given a normalized position x along the upper boundary section (1 at the cusp, 0 at white) and a curvature whose absolute value is less than 1, returning the normalized chroma at that position:

The boundary section is the arc of the circle which passes through (0, 0) and (1, 1) with the given signed curvature. Rather than locating the center of that circle, which is very far away when the curvature is close to 0, the circle’s equation is multiplied through by the curvature and solved directly for the chroma, which avoids subtracting large, nearly equal quantities.

steps.html: let <var>t</var> be sqrt(2 − <var>curvature</var>²)
let <var>b</var> be <var>t</var> − <var>curvature</var>
let <var>d</var> be <var>x</var> × (<var>t</var> + <var>curvature</var> × (1 − <var>x</var>))
let <var>disc</var> be max(0, <var>b</var>² + 4 × <var>curvature</var> × <var>d</var>)
return 2 × <var>d</var> / (<var>b</var> + sqrt(<var>disc</var>))

algorithms.name: to gamut map a color by Ray Tracing
algorithms.html:
To Ray Trace Gamut Map a color origin in color space origin color space to be in gamut of an RGB destination color space destination:
To cast a ray through a linear-light RGB space from start to end (in gamut mapping, start is an anchor within the RGB gamut and end is the gamut mapped color, on the cubical gamut surface):
14.2.6.1. Footnotes for Ray Trace algorithm

steps.html: if <var>destination</var> has no gamut limits (XYZ-D65, XYZ-D50, Lab, LCH, Oklab, OkLCh) convert <var>origin</var> to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color

let <var>origin_OkLCh</var> be <var>origin</var> converted from <var>origin color space</var>
			to the OkLCh color space

if the Lightness of <var>origin_OkLCh</var> is greater than or equal to 100%,
			convert `oklab(1 0 0 / origin.alpha)` to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color

if the Lightness of <var>origin_OkLCh</var> is less than than or equal to 0%,
			convert `oklab(0 0 0 / origin.alpha)` to <var>destination</var> and return it as the gamut mapped color
let <var>l_origin</var> be the OkLCh lightness component of <var>origin_OkLCh</var>
let <var>h_origin</var> be the OkLCh hue component of <var>origin_OkLCh</var>
let anchor be an achromatic OkLCh color formed with l_origin as lightness, 0 as chroma and h_origin as hue, converted to the linear-light form of destination
let origin_rgb be origin_OkLCh converted to the linear-light form of destination

if origin_rgb is not in gamut
  • let low be 0.0 + 1E-12 1
  • let high be 1.0 - 1E-12 2
  • let last be origin_rgb
  • for (i=0; i<4; i++)
    • if (i > 0)
      • let current_OkLCh be origin_rgb converted to OkLCh
      • let the lightness of current_OkLCh be l_origin
      • let the hue of current_OkLCh be h_origin 3
      • let origin_rgb be current_OkLCh converted to the linear-light form of destination
    • Cast a ray from start = anchor to end = origin_rgb and let intersection be the intersection of this ray with the gamut boundary
    • if an intersection was not found, let origin_rgb be last and exit the loop 5
    • if (i >0) AND (each component of origin_rgb is between low and high) then let anchor be origin_rgb 4
    • let origin_rgb be intersection
    • let last be intersection
set <var>clipped</var> to clip(<var>origin_rgb</var>)
return <var>clipped</var> as the gamut mapped color

algorithms.name: to gamut map a color by Ray Tracing
algorithms.html:
To <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-export="" id="cast-a-ray" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">cast a ray</dfn> through a linear-light RGB space
		from <var>start</var> to <var>end</var>
		(in gamut mapping,
		<var>start</var> is an anchor within the RGB gamut
		and <var>end</var> is the gamut mapped color, on the cubical gamut surface):

steps.html: let bmin and bmax be 3-element arrays with the gamut’s lower and upper bounds, respectively 6
let <var>tfar</var> be infinity (or some very large number)
let <var>tnear</var> be -infinity (or some very large, negative number)
let <var>direction</var> be a 3-element array

for (i = 0; i < 3; i++):
  • let a be start [i]
  • let b be end [i]
  • let d be b - a
  • let direction [i] be d
  • if abs(d) > 1E-12 7
    • let inv_d be 1 / d
    • let t1 be (bmin [i] - a ) * inv_d
    • let t2 be (bmax [i] - a ) * inv_d
    • let tnear be max(min(t1, t2), tnear )
    • let tfar be min(max(t1, t2), tfar )
  • else if (a < bmin[i] or a > bmax[i])
    • return INTERSECTION NOT FOUND

if (tnear > tfar or tfar < 0)
  • return INTERSECTION NOT FOUND

if tnear < 0
  • let tnear be tfar 8

if tnear is infinite (or matches the initial very large value)
  • return INTERSECTION NOT FOUND

for (i =0; i < 3; i++):
  • let result [i] be start [i] + direction [i] * tnear
return <var>result</var>
